neighbours.label: a hyphen-plus-consonant word piece ('-t', '-s', '-h', '-f') that starts the second half of a hyphenated compound (mid-twenties, left-hander, short-finned), versus the same words without the hyphen
fire: By her mid-thirties she had opened three bakeries.
He stopped mid-sentence when the phone rang.
The team signed a young left-hander last week.
The short-tailed weasel hunts mice in the snow.
The short-sighted plan failed within a year.
She paused mid-sip and looked up.
Our coach is a former right-hander from Ohio.
We spotted a short-horned lizard on the trail.
quiet: By her thirties she had opened three bakeries.
He stopped talking when the phone rang.
The team signed a young pitcher last week.
The small weasel hunts mice in the snow.
The careless plan failed within a year.
She paused for a moment and looked up.
Our coach is a former pitcher from Ohio.
We spotted a small lizard on the trail.
